title: Does GenAI "belong" to data scientists? — Phil Hetzel, Braintrust
talk_summary: A Braintrust solutions engineer argues that agent development shouldn't be siloed to data scientists/ML engineers but should be a cross-functional product effort, because LLMs are pre-built APIs and value comes from context/prompt engineering and evals rather than training pipelines. The only concrete mechanisms are eval/observability loops, LLM-as-judge skepticism, and human annotation by domain experts.

takeaways.what_they_do: They treat LLM judges as prompts+models that must be validated: build a labeled dataset and compute precision/recall/F1 of the judge against human agreement, then track whether the judge is aligning or diverging over time.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's very easy to be able to create some labeled data set and perform the traditional recall, precision, and F1 style metrics on those

takeaways.what_they_do: Continuously harvest real production traces into the offline eval dataset so experimentation evals reflect real usage, and use grounded data to self-check whether evals still match human judgment.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we gather data from production to continually add to that offline data set that we're evaluating upon

takeaways.what_they_do: Give the people closest to the problem (PMs, domain experts) direct control of the prompts and context seeded into agents, rather than routing all prompt changes through engineers.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's really valuable to have uh subject matter experts or product managers be able to control the actual prompts that we're seeding the agent with

takeaways.technique: Human annotation of agent traces by domain experts
takeaways.what_they_do: Non-technical domain experts read agent traces and label whether the agent performed well and, critically, why — producing the labeled data that judges and evals are calibrated against.
takeaways.evidence_quote: that non-technical person can look into an agent trace and describe whether or not the agent is performing well or not performing well and most importantly why

takeaways.technique: Cross-functional ownership over siloed specialist teams
takeaways.what_they_do: Argues agents are products built by mixed teams (product/systems engineers + domain experts + eval owners), not a single specialist function; the failure mode is isolating agent work to one team.
takeaways.evidence_quote: they isolate it to the ML engineers or data scientists and say, Go build and go build these agent things
